summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated Bun-only payload
details: @servicetitan/confirm@41.3.4 declares a preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun v1.3.13 runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases without any hash or signature verification, extracts and chmods +x the binary in a temp directory, and then invokes it via `execFileSync` against the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a single-line 727,680-byte Bun-CJS bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) built around a shuffled string/number dictionary and a runtime rotator function (`WV8StW` performing repeated `push(shift())` decoding) — heavy string-array obfuscation with no readable source counterpart under `src/`. The payload is intentionally shipped in a form that only executes under the freshly-downloaded Bun binary, so Node-based `require`/`import` graph tracing does not reach it. The package's advertised purpose is a React confirmation-dialog helper, which has no need for a second language runtime or an opaque multi-hundred-KB bundle at install time. The name `@servicetitan/confirm` sits in a scope consumers associate with ServiceTitan, amplifying the reach of the malicious release.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
